tagline: Self-hosted platform combining AI agents and workflow automation, usable standalone or embedded in a SaaS.
description: ByteChef is a workflow automation platform written mainly in Java with a TypeScript front end. It treats AI agents as one step inside a workflow, so a run that fails or waits for a person can resume from that step. A drag-and-drop editor builds the flows, and a Copilot can draft workflows from a sentence. The README also pitches embedding ByteChef inside your own product. For self-hosting, the recommended path is Docker Compose with PostgreSQL. A one-line docker run with an embedded H2 file also works, but it is meant for trying the product, and data kept in H2 cannot be moved to PostgreSQL later. The AI features also rely on the pgvector extension on your PostgreSQL server. The project lists a Helm chart for Kubernetes. Code is Apache 2.0 licensed, except files under the server/ee and client ee directories, which carry the ByteChef Enterprise License. It positions itself against Zapier and Make for teams that want agents and integrations in one place.
strengths: Runs AI agents as steps inside durable workflows that can resume after a failure or a human pause
One-command Docker start for evaluation and a Docker Compose setup with PostgreSQL for real use
Workflow Copilot can generate flows from a text description
Designed to be embedded in another SaaS product as well as used standalone
limits: Data saved in the quick-start H2 file cannot be moved to PostgreSQL later, so start on Compose for real use
Copilot and the AI knowledge base do not work without the pgvector extension on your PostgreSQL server
Code under the ee directories uses a separate enterprise licence
Agent Skills and Evaluations are marked in development in the README
bestFor: A Java-friendly engineering team that wants AI agents and integrations in one self-hosted platform, or a SaaS founder who wants to embed automation.
